assets.scope: dreadfell, halfling-ruins, collapsed-tower and amon-sul-crypt vault loots (undead/skeleton, default-name image, non-unique, no define_as, no nice_tile); the skeleton warrior/archer/mage siblings are separate shipped names

references.note: Approved disc, lighting and camera; do not copy its creature.
Native shape: a golden-ivory skeleton with both arms raised out to the sides, orange fire burning in each hand, blue ribbon sashes streaming around the ribs and legs.

Shipped skeleton mage (hunched skeleton wrapped in a dark blue-black cloak with a gold-lit skull): the magus is NOT cloaked; it is an open bare-boned figure with both arms raised, a flame in each hand and streaming cobalt ribbons.

prompt_fields.subject: A skeleton magus seen from a steep overhead three-quarter angle: a tall thin skeleton of warm ivory and pale gold bone standing upright and clearly open, with no cloak or hood, both arms bent with the forearms raised and the open hands held in front of the shoulders, a small bright orange-and-yellow flame burning just above each hand, a faint gold light in the eye sockets, short ribbon sashes of bright cobalt blue with pale-blue edges wrapping the ribcage and hips, small tarnished-gold trinkets on the wrists. Arcane, gaunt and complete.
prompt_fields.contrast: Skeleton family: the shipped skeleton mage is a hunched figure wrapped in a dark cloak, the skeleton warrior is a steel-armoured sword bearer, the archer is a bare skeleton drawing a bow. The magus is the OPEN upright bare-boned figure with both hands raised in front of the shoulders and a flame above each hand, wrapped in cobalt-blue ribbons (silhouette: upright bare skeleton, two hand flames at shoulder height, no cloak; hue: ivory-gold bone with cobalt and orange accents; value: light).
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Disc plate discipline: measured results show generations of this style reference tend to render the disc DARKER than the reference, never lighter. So do not darken the disc at all: render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band and the area under the creature -- at the style reference's own brightness, if anything a hair lighter, and never darker. No warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette anywhere on the disc. Do not darken the creature to compensate either. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures. Calibration from the previous generations of this exact token: with the arms raised in a wide V the hand flames reached past the disc edge (or, when drawn cautiously, the whole figure came out tiny). This time change the pose: both arms bent at the elbows, forearms raised, both open hands held in front of the shoulders about a hand-width apart, a small bright flame burning just above each hand, the ribbon sashes short and wrapped close around the ribs and hips. The figure is upright and compact and fills about three quarters of the disc radius around the disc centre, leaving a clear bare charcoal ring of base plate on every side.
prompt_fields.palette: Light warm ivory and pale-gold bone, bright cobalt-blue ribbons, orange and yellow hand flames; nothing darker than mid tone except the eye sockets and rib gaps; the hand flames must not cast orange light, glow or warm cast onto the disc, which stays neutral charcoal. Dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel, kept a visibly lighter value than the creature's darkest parts so the two never merge.
